name: DAEdeltaALUS
full_name: Decay-At-rest Experiment for delta-CP studies At the Laboratory for Underground Science
summary: DAEdeltaALUS was a proposed multi-source decay-at-rest programme to measure the leptonic CP phase. Its original concept paired three cyclotron-driven neutrino sources with a very large underground detector. IsoDAR developed as a related lower-energy source programme.
physics_targets: Leptonic CP violation through antineutrino appearance
detection_principle: Protons produce positive pions that stop and decay, followed by positive-muon decay. The resulting muon antineutrinos would oscillate to electron antineutrinos, detected through inverse beta decay. Source timing and different source distances separate the oscillation samples.

sites.name: Original DUSEL / Homestake candidate implementation
sites.location: Lead, South Dakota; source sites around the proposed detector

status.label: Proposed
status.evidence: The expression of interest and source paper describe an unbuilt proposal, with no full DAEdeltaALUS neutrino exposure established. The INFN directory classifies it among expired projects.

timeline.event: Expression of interest released for a CP-violation programme associated with DUSEL.

collaboration.name: DAEdeltaALUS Collaboration
collaboration.participants_note: Institutions listed here are selected documented participants; the official collaboration page provides the complete membership.

key_parameters.name: Source baselines
key_parameters.value: 1.5 km, 8 km and 20 km in the original design

key_parameters.name: Cyclotron concept
key_parameters.value: Molecular-hydrogen acceleration to 800 MeV per nucleon with stripping extraction

key_parameters.name: Appearance channel
key_parameters.value: Muon antineutrino to electron antineutrino, observed by inverse beta decay

results.summary: Published a multi-baseline source concept and forecast CP sensitivity; no DAEdeltaALUS oscillation result is claimed.

science_scope: This dossier preserves a named historical proposal. Design parameters and sensitivity estimates are not measured neutrino results; later programmes using the same laboratory or technology are distinct.
